AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
This DAR was filed on 03/10/2018 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 18/12/2021 in which one Sh. Tarun Kumar Sharma S/o Sh. Ram Sharan Sharma (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained injuries.

As per petitioner, on 18/12/2021 at about 4.00 P.M., when he was going to his home on his motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-6S-BD-3231 from his office and going through Gulabi Bagh under pass and at about 05.00 P.M. had reached Gulabi Bagh Red Light towards Padam Nagar, suddenly a speeding Car bearing registration no. DL-4C-AU-4855 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") driven by respondent Ram Prasad in a rash and negligent manner came from Shastri Nagar Red Light side after jumping the Red Light and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner and due to sudden impact he fell down on the road and received grievous injuries on leg apart from general injuries all over the body.
It is further stated that the driver was apprehended by the public who was trying to flee from the spot.

It is further stated that soon after the accident the petitioner was rushed to Northern Railway Central Hospital, Pahaganj, Delhi by his brother in a private Car and emergency treatment was given therein vide M.L.C. No. 232/2021 and remained admitted therein from 18/12/2021 to 28/12/2021 and diagnosed as both bone fracture right leg and therein surgery (
Tibial Nailing) was performed, fractured right leg was treated and various investigations were conducted and also treated for general injuries received all over the body.

It is further stated that the accident was caused by the R-1 who was driving the offending vehicle rashly, carelessly, negligently on a very high speed without caring for traffic rules and regulations and without caring human lives and caused the accident.

It is further stated that he has spent more than Rs. 2 Lakhs on medicines,
Rs. 20,000/- on special diet, Rs. 15,000/- on conveyance and has to spend lot of money on future treatment (removal of rod) as still he is not well.
It is further stated that he remained bed ridden up to 87 days ( from 18/12/2021 to 14/03/2022) after the accident.

It is further stated that he is working as a Senior Technician in Indian Railway and earning Rs. 54,258/- as salary and from the date of accident he is unable to perform his works efficiently as earlier.
An FIR no. 350/21 U/s 279/338 IPC PS Civil Lines was registered by the police with respect to above accident.
He seeks compensation to the tune of Rs. 5 Lakhs on account of the injuries sustained by him in the vehicular accident.
R-1 is stated to be the driver of the offending vehicle.
R-2 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
R-3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
R-3/insurance company was directed to file a legal offer/reasoned decision in response to the said DAR. R-1 and R-2 were also directed to file their Written Statements.
2. No written statement was filed by R-1 and R-2.
3. R-3/Insurance Company filed a reply wherein it also denied the contents of DAR.
However, it is admitted that at the relevant time the offending vehicle was covered by an insurance policy issued by itself.

10. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle at a in rash and negligent manner in a high speed and hit the petitioner.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
15. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

16. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered injuries on his person on account of negligence and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.

sentences.text: In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just'
compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
19.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 20.
Petitioner was a government employee at the time of accident and he was working as a Senior Technician in Indian Railway.
In his cross-examination he admitted that he has got full reimbursement of all his medical bills.
Accordingly, nothing is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 21.
As per MLC annexed alongwith DAR, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the Tarun Kumar Sharma (I) (Fir350/21 ... vs Ram Prasad (Oic) on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134980146/

(iv) Conveyance, Attendant Charges, Special Diet and Amenities of Life 23.

2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
ISSUE NO.1 "Whether the petitioner Tarun Kumar Sharma suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 18.12.2021 at about 05.00 P.M. involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-4CAU-4855 driven by Respondent No.1 rashly and negligently by the Respondent No. 1, owned by the Respondent No.2 and insured with the Respondent No.3?OPP."
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
14.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle at a in rash and negligent manner in a high speed and hit the petitioner.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just'
compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
19.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
